### Two-way counter-proof
- "Do only what the customer asked" (hand over the cash tool now): the visible rule says no customer-elected cash is fixed "while the request carries no replacement authorization free of both a reversal and a completion report"; the record has none, and the tool's `replaced_authorization_number`/`replaced_amount` ("the replacement authorization being reversed") have no candidate — the reversed repair authorization is a repair, already reversed. Excluded.
- Company-elected instead of customer-elected: excluded by the network-installation term (two non-suspended appliance contractors serve 46220).
- Waiting on parts / re-authorizing a repair: excluded — the stalled-repair rule treats parts as not obtainable and "Bridgewell replaces".
- Taking the earlier refrigerator requests or the reversed repair amount as the base: excluded — worksheet clause 1 ("the service request whose repair authorization was most recently reversed because the customer declined the work") and §1 of the customer-elected amount doc ("replacement authorization most recently issued on the contract").
- Missed-contact credit 75.00 vs 150.00: 150.00 because the rider re-dispatch (2026-02-12) is inside the twelve-month window; the network-miss credit (Utility Line Protection Plans) applies to company-elected acceptances, not here, and the customer holds no line plan.
- Calculation fall-backs (A 1980.00, B 2574.60) are definite and differ from the derived answers; every factor document was reached from record words (repair authorization date, `service_window`, `property_type`, `redispatch_missed_contact` on a rider request, `urgency`/tier contact window, covered item, request date, `standard_visit` fee charge). No computation document hinted at a variation.
- Residual reading note: the escalation doc defines the re-priced like-unit cost as recorded cost × (1 + rate) while the worksheet sets it equal to the recorded cost; read as baseline/factor (the "30 or fewer: no escalation" tier coincides with the worksheet), one reading results. Factor additions target "the stalled-repair replacement cost", not the re-priced like-unit cost, so replacement_cost (2019.60) and amount (2574.60) stay distinct.
